public_rationale: The evidence does not settle whether the named systems connect language to real-world referents as of 25 April 2025 [e1–e3]. The LaMDA paper, available on 10 February 2022, documents next-token pretraining; this establishes its training objective, not the absence of semantic representations [e1]. The July 2020 position paper argues that training on linguistic form cannot yield meaning, but does not empirically test the named systems [e2]. Anthropic's 27 March 2025 report describes interventions on Claude's geographical representations that changed its answers, challenging a simple word-association account without independently establishing semantic grounding [e3]. LaMDA's source-attribution measures also do not settle whether its design seeks semantic reference, so the assertion that these systems make no such effort remains unresolved [e1].
limitations: The evidence supplies no decisive test separating semantic reference from sophisticated linguistic associations [e1–e3].
The Claude findings come from its developer, cover selected tasks, and use a method acknowledged to capture only part of the computation and potentially introduce artifacts [e3].
The evidence does not establish the full capabilities or design of the unspecified Claude version intended by the claim.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Language models like LaMDA do not connect their representations to the world; they are just autocomplete that predicts which words fit a context.

statement.excerpt: Software like LaMDA simply doesn’t; it doesn’t even try to connect to the world at large, it just tries to be the best version of autocomplete it can be, by predicting what words best fit a given context.
statement.document_title: New adventures in AI hype: “Our language models are so ‘conscious’ we need to give them rights”

Search and replace LaMDA with Claude, and it all still applies.
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading in context concerns semantic understanding: whether these systems relate language to the things and situations it describes. It is not merely a claim that they cannot retrieve external text.

The autocomplete description asserts a limitation on what the systems learn and do, not merely the use of a next-token prediction objective. That objective alone cannot establish the asserted limitation.

Evidence of semantic grounding need not establish consciousness or require human-like sensory experience. Conversely, retrieving sources or producing fluent answers does not by itself establish semantic understanding.

I assess the ongoing assertion as of the post date, 2025-04-25. There is no regular reporting period for this property. The June 2022 passage supplies historical context; earlier studies are retained as context rather than assigned new event dates.

The words 'doesn’t even try' concern whether the system's design seeks semantic connection. The developer's use of the label 'groundedness' is insufficient unless its operational meaning matches that connection.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence about the named systems establishes that their apparent reference to things and situations is confined to associations among linguistic forms, without representations that track and are used to reason about those referents. Design evidence must also support the asserted absence of an effort toward semantic connection. A prediction objective or isolated failures alone would not establish this.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reproducible behavioral and mechanistic evidence establishes that a named system uses representations tied to real-world referents or situations across changes in wording and context, addressing explanations based only on surface associations. For the design assertion, evidence must show an effort toward semantic reference, rather than merely source attribution. Retrieval alone does not meet either test.

evidence.explanation: This establishes the prediction objective, not the absence of semantic representations. The paper also describes fine-tuning and external tools, but its source-based groundedness does not by itself settle Marcus's semantic claim.

This provides a substantive argument consistent with Marcus's distinction between word sequences and meaning. It predates the named systems and is not an empirical demonstration that they lack semantic understanding; availability is conservatively recorded at the end of the proceedings' dated conference.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Controlled behavioral and mechanistic studies of the relevant versions showing whether representations track independently specified real-world referents and causally support reasoning across changes in wording and context. These studies must distinguish semantic reference from linguistic association. Design documentation must separately establish whether the systems pursue semantic connection beyond source attribution; evidence supporting categorical absence must go beyond isolated failures.
